hypothesis: After an OECD leading-indicator peak (trough), the central bank cuts (hikes) within 6 months more often than it does after any month.
knownLimits: The leading indicator is today's vintage: the OECD revises past months, so turns are dated with some hindsight.
A turn is two months one way then two months the other (the app's own rule), dated when the second month after it is published.
Every country the app covers with both a BIS monthly policy rate and an OECD leading indicator is pooled; countries with pegs or long holds lower the base rate.
Cases are treated as independent in the p-value; turns in the same country are months apart, but global cycles make countries move together.
